ADHD, anxiety disorder, heart disease, blood clotting disorder, etc.

But since January I have been having symptoms that don't fit with those. I started trying to keep up with them, but kept forgetting. AND THEN, I remembered BEARABLE.

Being able to add any symptoms I'm having has made a huge difference!! I have a record to show the doctor. She was amazed. I had dates, timelines, symptoms, and everything that was different than usual, like I forgot to eat, how many trips to the ladies room, what I ate, my mood and as many as you need to add for your particular situation. The doctor ordered a MRI and appropriate blood test. I found out that I don't have what I thought but I was heard by my doctor.

Bear is easy to setup and use, even a reminder so you don't forget. It's worth getting and using.
The reports tell you and your doctor how you are doing.

reviews.title: Time consuming for little data feedback
reviews.text:
I've been using this app for two years, as a paid user for the first year. I initially started using it to test it out for someone with chronic health conditions who is taking about 30 medications per day. I've been using it to track my own medical conditions and mental health.

This app causes me more anxiety just to use it. It requires me to fill out dozens and dozens of symptoms at different ratings twice a day. That would be perfectly OK if I felt that I was getting good or even average interpreted information on the app that explained correlations of my symptoms. Hopefully that would in turn, allow me to know when I will have a flareup or know what factors to avoid that lead to increased symptoms.

My entire purpose of using the app is to hopefully understand how some of my symptoms correlate and to be able to reduce their severity. In terms of using it to track mental health symptoms, it's even more depressing to get through with a tough day and have an app that gives you absolutely no coping mechanism or positive messages for solutions to any of the symptoms that you're going through. Understandably, it is a tracking app and not a treatment app. 

The app has a lot of great customizability and features, however for my uses I have concluded after two years that it is not worth my time and I will return to my previous methods. My friend didn't end up downloading it either because they were not interested in having to fill out so much information every day.

reviews.title: The Best Health Tracking App I’ve Found
reviews.text:
I’ve tried a lot of health tracking apps over the years, and Bearable is by far my favorite. As someone living with multiple chronic illnesses, it’s incredibly helpful to have one place to track symptoms, pain, sleep, medications, mood, energy, vitals, and so much more.

What really sets Bearable apart is its flexibility. You can customize almost everything to fit your own health conditions and daily routine. I also love the insights feature, which helps identify patterns and possible triggers that I might never have noticed on my own. Those reports have been useful not only for me but also when discussing my health with my doctors.

The developers are constantly improving the app and genuinely listen to feedback from the community. If you’re looking for a powerful, customizable health tracker that can grow with your needs, I highly recommend Bearable. It’s become an essential part of managing my health. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

reviews.title: Supportive aid
reviews.text:
I can’t say enough good things about the Bearable app. As someone dealing with chronic pain and day-to-day health challenges, this app has genuinely been a game changer for me.

It’s incredibly easy to use, but also very detailed—you can track symptoms, mood, sleep, medications, and so much more all in one place. What really stands out is how it helps you start to see patterns over time. Things I never would have connected on my own suddenly make more sense, and that’s empowering.

It doesn’t feel overwhelming like some health apps can. Instead, it feels supportive—like a tool that’s actually built for people who are trying to understand their bodies better, not just collect data.

Honestly, it’s helped me feel a little more in control of my health, and that’s something I really needed. I would absolutely recommend it to anyone managing chronic illness, mental health, or even just wanting better insight into their daily wellbeing.

reviews.text:

Other gripes:
- factors in the calendar view don’t include things like sleep quality or duration.
- lifestyle factors like alcohol, caffeine, etc are bucketed into ‘a lot,’ ‘a little’ etc which is how you report them, but to not be able to just overlay ‘alcohol’ as a concept vs having to do ‘alcohol: a little’ etc is just asinine. 

Overall just feels like this is built for vibey people to give them feely goodies and not for people actually interested in bio hacking and statistics. The features that would unlock a power user are not big tho, so idk what gives.

reviews.title: Excellent - but with room to improve
reviews.text:
I needed a symptom tracker and wanted one with additional features I could use to record and understand my condition. Bearable fit the bill and I do believe it is the best option for me! It is very adaptable and granular, which are among many traits I love.
But I was slightly disappointed in a few ways others should consider before choosing this app...
I think its adaptability works against it in some cases, as the interface is rarely optimal for the current task. If there was a focused view that opened with the relavent notification, that would make things like logging meds a little faster (it does for check-ins but nothing else afaik). The check ins are also a little confusing and convolute with other features. But it's perfectly manageable, and I understand that this type of development is rightfully often a low priority.
Similarly, it is hard to make cumulative edits. If you accidentally enter data on the wrong date, which can be easy to do, there is no way to move/copy it other than manually.
Finally, I understood the app to have more in terms of task management and journaling. It sort of has both, but you get more of a routine/goal reminder than a to do list, and 'journaling' is in the form of optional (usually Premium) notes. These are also a "cherry on top" features, but I interpreted the description as including these.

It's a great app and I'm grateful for the developers! I give 4 stars considering that a good and honest rating. I believe these points are being addressed already, and I intend to update my review as features evolve.

reviews.text:

they’ve changed the format and now it’s way harder to add a one off symptom than it should be. this was a big one for me, because the one offs are more insightful at times than the daily things I go thru. I immediately cancelled my subscription. The kind of people using this app don’t have bandwidth to tinker with settings every time something changes. I don’t want to join discord or read the subreddit. I’m a Gen-Xennial with chronic pain - I just want the app to serve its purpose without complicating my existence.

Dec. 2025
My doctor asked me to start tracking symptoms so we can further narrow a few things down in my chronic illness journey. I’m too forgetful to go the notebook route, so the reminders to check in have been great and I love the customization capabilities for symptom tracking. If I could add anything to it, I’d like the ability to track symptoms thru the day - ie if my back pain starts at noon, I’d like to pop into the app and mark that down. Right now I get a pop up that says “This will mark (symptom) for all day - are you sure” (or something along those lines.)
I’d rather have a time stamp for when I entered the symptom like there are for other things the app tracks.
EDIT TO ADD: developer response helped me fix the timing issue - I missed that setting.
I would still like a fuller & more reliable integration with Apple Health. My watch tracks so many things that could feed into the app, but don’t.
Other than that - I’m a happy camper.

reviews.title: Easy to use, but privacy is a dealbreaker
reviews.text:
I used Bearable for well over a year and there’s a lot to like. The app is easy to use, the interface is friendly, and the tracking is fairly customizable. It’s a simple way to log symptoms and keep everything in one place.

That said, I was originally hoping for more meaningful insights. The correlations I got mostly confirmed things I already suspected, and over time the effort of recording symptoms every day started to feel like more hassle than it was worth.

What ultimately pushed me to stop using Bearable was privacy. My iPhone’s App Privacy Report showed the app regularly contacting a Facebook domain, even though I don’t use Facebook to log in. For a health‑related app, that’s a hard no for me. If the developers ever remove those trackers and take a more privacy‑first approach, I’d be open to giving it another try - but in its current state, I’m out.

reviews.title: LOVE this app (and want a little more)
reviews.text:
I love this app. It’s been very helpful in managing symptoms and treatment for my menstrual cycle, mental health, lupus and any other cold, pain or illness that comes up. It’s user friendly and offers a good deal of customization. I appreciate the reports it’s able to generate and will likely be using this app for a long time. That said, I’d love to see a few improvements especially around the medication tracking. It would be super helpful to: 
- be able to save dosage instructions for each medication in the app
- set reminders based on a set number of hours you have to wait before taking another dose. for example: if i mark having taken Tylenol at 11am, it could automatically set a reminder for me to take it again at 5pm. Or at least let me make a note on the medication for how often I can take it. 
- be able to set/save MAX dosing info (ie. I’ve taken 4 out of my allotted 6 Tylenol today)

In terms of tracking symptoms, it would be very helpful to be able to mark the time symptoms start / stop, worsen or change. 

And in terms of nutrition, having the option to track or at least save the amount of protein, fat, carbs, fiber, etc I’ve had during every meal / every day would be a game changer. So much of chronic illness deals with diet, I’d just love to see more capabilities here. 

All in all though- this app is amazing. I notice a huge difference in my discipline and overall health when I am consistently using it, and I will always recommend it to friends /family. My requests are simply geared towards allowing me to use this app MORE. If I could manage everything in one magical place (and have that place be Bearable), life managing everything would be just a weeeeeee bit easier 🙏🏾

reviews.title: If You’ve Got The Time
reviews.text:
It’s definitely an all in one health care tracking app but it’s super complex and takes a lot of time to setup and then to do your check in two to three times a day. There’s a lot of complicated areas of the app and I would only recommend it to people who are really interested in tracking every aspect of their health journey. That being said it’s difficult to setup, missing options and limiting options on being better at tracking specific health issues. You really have to go out of your way to manually setup how you want to track the illness and it doesn’t really give you the ability to design a system around your specific disease. 

To be honest, I’d just stick to a handwritten journal if you want to really create your own system for tracking your very specific health care and plan, the mood you’re in, and so forth. This app just just is too complicated, takes a lot of time to setup, and doesn’t even offer ways to track side effects, tracking how you’re progressing, and for me I just don’t see the value in it with the amount of time it takes to get through your check ins or even offering everything you should track based on your health issue.

reviews.title: So helpful
reviews.text:
I love Bearable. When I first installed the app I chose to track basically everything I possibly could, but didn’t upgrade to premium. I tracked for about three months and didn’t look at any of my data because it was difficult to consume all the charts and graphs without the ease of premium telling me “your mood is generally worse when you have a migraine” and so on. Then I got premium in a Black Friday deal and have been amazed by the correlations Bearable has put together. I 100% recommend this app, and suggest you to track as much as you can! (Without getting stressed about it.) Taking time to do morning and evening check-ins every day for consistency has really changed my chronic illness journey as I’m able to see potential triggers and things that help. 
The only downside I can see to this app is that I haven’t found a way to track the local weather and how it may relate to your symptoms. I would love an update with this!

reviews.title: Pretty good - some UI suggestions for accessibility
reviews.text:
I LOVE the variety of options and wide customization so that I don’t need separate apps, however, the process of entering all of that data has become quite tedious.

It would be nice to have options to describe the qualities of the pain (like burning or sharp) and be able to select multiple locations (rather than having to have separate items for facial pain and hand pain). I use this app for most of the available features, so I think it would be nice to have an option to have different tabs for those aspects—and then select from a customized list of items—rather than have to create new ones and scroll down a long line of lists. I find the selectable options (as in your food tracking and mood tabs) much easier and quicker to use.

Also would much appreciate being able to send the data I input here to Apple Health, and being able to import my water data from Apple Health…and track amounts of drinks other than water.

The interface is cute and not too clinical; it’d also be great for tweens or teens with chronic conditions. Highly recommend!

reviews.title: I don’t review things often…but this app is AMAZING!
reviews.text: I have been dealing with gallbladder, gallbladder, removal, surgery, and severe gastrointestinal issues for the last year. I am very young still at the age of 34. I have been waiting an appointment with a G.I. doctor for the last several months while my symptoms have continued to worsen and I’ve dropped a lot of weight, I am vomiting every day, amongst many other things. This is affecting my ability to work as well as I usually do because I am a workaholic through and through… Needless to say, I have been struggling pretty badly and have an already anxious predisposition when it comes to health issues. This app has single-handedly given me the ability to track my symptoms with such great detail that I am confident I will have a record of my symptoms to provide the G.I. doctor when my appointment happens in December. I decided to pay for the yearly upgrade, but even without that the free version was amazing! reviews.text:
I haven’t been using this application very long. So, far I like it very much. 

It’s easier to keep track of what I’ve eaten and how much I drink. I just wish there was a way to log other liquids besides water and that the ounces were more flexible in adjustment. 

Sometimes, I drink a 16 ounce glass of Mimosa or lemon water and other times during the day, I might drink an 8 ounce glass of plain mineral water or a 12 ounce mug of tea or hot chocolate.  

That’s why I deducted two stars. There’s no way to adjust between 8, 12, 16, 20 or other liquid ounce measurements or log other liquid types by name. 

I do like being able to keep track of the physical manifestations I experience along with blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, mood, energy levels, sleep and gratitude. Very nice! 

My primary care physician strongly suspects I have a progressive type of MS. I have been wanting an application such as this one to notate everything I mentioned. Now, I can show her and my neurologist what’s going on with me. Hopefully, it will lead to me actually being diagnosed with it before the year ends. 

I wish I had the funds available for the full version of this application. If I had the money, I might get it.

reviews.title: Takes some getting used to.
reviews.text:
I'm only on my second day and have barely touched the app and they're asking for a review. Do you love it? Do you just love it? Wellllll... I've barely used it so I can't really give an honest or objective review but you asked so here it goes. 

Im currently only using the free version and there's A LOT to unpack. This is a good thing because if I want to track my health, my disease, my symptoms, my moods and/or my medications I want A LOT to choose from. But I'm trying to get used to all this information and what and where to enter. And it's everywhere. Without time or reason. There is much room for improvement here which is why I may not go with the paid version. It needs more coherence and ease of cross reference. 

One example: I took my evening meds and after 2 hours still couldn't sleep so I  got up took another medication. When I went to record it, I can only enter that I took 2 tablets. Not that I took another hours later. I wouldn't want to look back and thinki took double my dose right out the gate. That's not even remotely helpful in tracking symptoms. It's confusing actually. 

I'd like a daily time line to look at maybe like a calendar So I can see what happened with everything throughout the day at a glance and not need to go through all the prompts. Maybe that's in there and I just haven't found it. 

That's the problem with asking for reviews after literally 5 minutes of use... You haven't given me time to appreciate your app.

UPDATE: After a few days I joined the 7day free trial. There’s A LOT to unpack here and while this has potential to be one of the most helpful apps out there, they have a lot of improvement to do to lessen confusion. For example. Listing medications are in paragraph form causing dosing numbers to run together causing confusion when simply listing them line by line would clear that up. They gave a toggle system but you’re not toggling to show the task has been done. Or still needs to be done. A bullet system here might be better. I’m a retired graphic designer so I have much cleaner and cohesive ideas for this. Right now there’s much room for improvement.

reviews.title: Easiest app I’ve tried
reviews.text: I’ve loved this app so far. It’s definitely the easiest tracking app I’ve had, especially since it automatically gets some data from my Fitbit. I feel like you do have to get the premium for this app to even matter, and I hate premiums, but it was so cheap I figured it was worth it to start keeping track of all my different health problems. It’s extremely customizable so I’m able to keep track of ALL of my different symptoms, all in one app which is SO useful and helps me actually keep track instead of just having too low of energy to care enough. It just doesn’t show my heart rate on a graph, or at least I haven’t figured out where, but I just use cardiogram free for that, which isn’t much of a bother. reviews.text: This app is making it easy for me to track so much pertinent data in one place. Been using it for almost two weeks now. Still trying to figure out how to use it in some respects, but it’s very helpful to have the notifications, helps me remember to track things I would normally forget. Just getting the data recorded is half the battle. I appreciate the different methods you can set to record info but wish more options were available for more data points. I especially like the new set up for the daily check in, it makes it so much easier to find each section and record data quickly before I can forget. Thank you to the creators and team!

reviews.text: I’ve never written an app review before but I needed to give Bearable 5 stars. It has made such a different in my life. I have chronic migraine which comes with a whole slew of symptoms many of which are constantly changing. Bearable helps me keep track of how I’m feeling as well as track any correlations, which is a total game changer and something I always wished I could do!!! I’ve recommended it to everyone and all my doctors. Hands down the best app I’ve ever used for my migraines. I love the bear, that is super cute and love to see it when I feel bad. reviews.title: Really helpful app

I am terrible at tracking data consistently but find bearable reminders and UI easy to use and have been successful tracking data for about a month. The correlations are helpful as are the graphs.

reviews.title: I ♥️ Lists and Rating Systems
reviews.text:
This app (ESPECIALLY for the price: ~$40/yr right now I think?) allows you to do so much and to customize so much. 

If the number of list items seems too many and is overwhelming, you can hide them. One of the absolute best features of Bearable is that you can write in your own items and your own lists, AND you can choose to do them on two types of ranking scales or simply a yes/no. 

For someone with chronic migraine disorder and a complicated slew of other autoimmune symptoms, I really don’t think I could ask for something better than this!! 

I hope more than anything they don’t end up doing the gradual price increases that lead to high prices before you know it, as some of my other apps have done. As it is right now (April 2025), I am so happy for this app as it is.

reviews.title: I replaced 12 apps w/ this ONE app that does it all better & more affordably
reviews.text:
I got this app because I’d heard it was good for managing chronic illness. And it very much is! Bearable has already helped me make some correlations that have improved my quality of life— things I wouldn’t have noticed on my own. 

But within this mission lie several functionalities that I was previously using multiple apps to attend to. (And it was becoming unwieldy! There comes a point when you’re spending more time setting up and updating apps than actually living your life, especially if you have some sort of executive dysfunction.) Bearable offers a multitude of functions that other apps offer as their *sole* function (and charge large monthly fees for).

And it is so entirely customizable that you can track all of your health issues in its single interface. Sleep patterns, pain, GI issues, energy, cognition, mood, allergies, heart issues, menstruation or menopause, weight loss, body measurements, hydration, dietary habits and suspected troublesome foods, exercise, autoimmune or eczema flares— anything you want to track, you can, along with potential influencing factors (again, customizable). And if it has a corollary in Apple Health, you can have the entries sync with each other. 

I also really appreciate the optional inclusion of what many other health apps leave out— social and lifestyle factors such as being outdoors (and the weather), time spent with friends/ partner/ family, screen time and video games, alcohol and caffeine intake, and any custom habits you suspect could be having an effect on your overall wellbeing. 

The yearly subscription fee is totally reasonable for this all-in-one bundle of functionality. There is a dedicated subreddit where the developer participates and is very responsive to feedback and suggestions, and where the enthusiastic user base makes it clear that this app has improved the health and lives of countless people. I’m so grateful that I found Bearable.

reviews.title: Easy, valuable, worth every penny
reviews.text:
The free version is amazing on its own, but I'm a data junkie, so I chose to invest in a year of premium, and I haven't regretted it for a second. The value this app brings is worth every cent. Especially since I got it while it was on sale (which I hear it frequently is) for a very low price.

TL;DR - This app is highly customizable, user friendly, and feature rich. Comes with all kinds of data visualizations, simple AND advanced, for maximum insight without being hard to understand.

Life changing:
- Detailed insights allow me to identify triggers, patterns, and other data that can provide insight on my symptoms. I can see who has the most positive impact on my life, which habits are truly serving their purpose, and whether any new medications are actually improving my symptoms. PLUS I can see which symptom management techniques are most effective, what time of day or day of the week I feel worst, and how my symptoms fluctuate over time. And more!
- The app provides suggestions for the best ways to manage your symptoms and the worst triggers to avoid, based on data from past logs. You can also input your own symptom management strategies for bad days. 
- Built-in (optional) medication tracking and reminders help me stay on top of which meds I take when, and make sure I never miss a day.
- Optional nutrition and water tracking also allows you to stay on top of your health and make sure you're meeting your needs. (I don't personally use this feature, but I can think of a thousand ways this could be helpful for other users.)

Practical upsides:
- User-friendly and easy to understand. I figured it out and set it up quickly.
- VERY customizable to allow the user to measure and track whatever you'd like, going as simple or in depth as your heart desires.
- Customizable reminders for the best times of day that work for you.
- Simple AND advanced data visualization at any time to best suit your needs.
- Low friction; it's so easy and simple to log symptoms that I find myself naturally doing it 5-10 times a day without reminders. Just tap a button and you're golden. 
- Community focused developers who take suggestions from the users and work hard to make the app better and better. Public suggestion forum includes information on plans for future changes.

Cons:
- Mood is rated on a scale of 1-10 and can be logged as many times per day as you'd like, but other symptoms are rated 0-4 and only up to 4 times per day in time blocks that are not customizable. I personally only care to rate my energy levels in detail, so I was able to work around this by just using the mood tracking section for energy levels instead. But this could be an issue for others.
- Due to the small development team, updates and new features may be slow.
- Does not currently have a built-in menstrual cycle tracker. (But it may in the future?)

THESE OPINIONS ARE MY OWN. I am not being paid or otherwise rewarded to say this.

reviews.title: Lots of potential but not quite there
reviews.text: I have been using this app every day for 4 months now. It has been ok for keeping track of things (although I’d like to track my symptom onset time with more specificity than 6 hour blocks), but not great for insights. First of all, their correlations grid does not give correlation values, and while that probably doesn’t bother most people, the results and conclusions can be misleading. Also, the 6 hour blocks in which things are tracked make it impossible to discover / distinguish for example migraine symptoms vs. migraine warning signs vs. migraine triggers because I don’t know in what order they happened, just that they all happened in “MID”. The data will still be good for analyzing other larger daily patterns though, like whether my migraines are related to allergies. ~~ I finally downloaded all my data to analyze it myself, and discovered there’s no way to get *all* of your data because it doesn’t export when you marked a symptom as “none” (even they know that unmeasured is not the same as 0, which is why their “Insights” analysis page encourages you to mark symptoms as none when they’re not active instead of leaving them blank). I tried to ask about how to get all of my data using the “Ask support” button under FAQs, but the button doesn’t work. I tried to report this as a bug, but it turns out the “Report a bug” button doesn’t work either 🤣

reviews.title: Life saver!!!
reviews.text:
I LOVE this app!!! It has seriously made keeping track of my laundry list of health problems so much easier. It’s also helped me improve other areas of my life that I didn’t anticipate when I first downloaded the app, I feel so much more aware and on track with the things in my day to day life. My lifestyle habits have improved, I am able to keep track of everything my doctors need, and I have found correlations in my habits and health that have made me more aware/able to improve my health! Aside from that, it has taken SO much stress out of my health tracking due to it being easy to use, insightful, and reliable. I would recommend this to anyone looking to improve their well being! 

The only reasons I gave this app 3 stars are;

1) The app isn’t the best when you are stuck behind a paywall. After paying, the app is stellar! I just hate subscriptions though and I wish I could pay once and be done with it. I don’t mind paying to support the creators of such a great app, it’s just not ideal that I am going to need to budget over $30+ for this for years. Considering that it’s a yearly payment instead of a monthly, that does help! However, as a girl on a tight budget, it’s not the easiest for me. 

2) This app doesn’t include menstrual cycle tracking, which would be SOOOO incredibly useful! My cycle/hormones have a BIG affect on my other health problems. It’s hard to keep track of the correlations between my health problems and where I am at in my cycle, and it would save me a lot of time if Bearable had a cycle tracking section that could show insights and correlations to/with everything else I track in the app. I use Stardust instead for cycle tracking (awesome app btw) but it is time consuming and somewhat difficult to go through each app and dig through entires to find correlations. I would feel much better about paying for this app if it included cycle tracking (especially since it affects around 50% of the populations health).

reviews.title: Helps with health anxiety
reviews.text:
I’m new to Bearable and have used it for one week. While I love bio-hacking as a concept, I have had difficulty tracking symptoms due to increasing health anxiety as I age. 

The older I get, the worse I feel physically, which in turn impacts my emotional wellbeing. It’s been difficult to face these challenges alone and I was pretty resistant to using Bearable when I first began because it has SO many metrics to keep track of. 

While this is a plus of the app, I was concerned it would be too overwhelming for me to learn. Fortunately that wasn’t the case. 

So far I’ve found it very easy to use and I truly appreciate the levels of tracking (low detail, medium detail, and high detail). This “low bar" to entry and the helpful tips built into the app helped me overcome anxiety and avoidance as I endeavor to improve my overall health. 

Easy, not stressful to use, and I can start slow and build up to tracking more details at my own pace. 👍

I also liked the well written privacy policy.
It is difficult to know which apps to trust with my private health information, but after reading through their privacy policies I feel reassured that Bearable is trustworthy.

I feel more empowered to take care of my health each time I check in with the app. Thank you Bearable team!

reviews.text: Can’t create an account if the keyboard doesn’t pop up when you try and type in a password. Why tell me to contact you again. I’ve reported it either fix it or don’t. I’m not going to spend my time holding your hand to support your app.

reviews.title: Amazing, dynamic app
reviews.text:
This app is very dynamic, and it’s getting more and more so. You have many options of ways to handle tracking your health. The devs are kind and helpful and so interactive with the community. They ask for feedback on designs and ideas and listen when people ask for certain features. 

This is the best health tracking app I’ve come across in my years of searching. 

As a minor suggestion for the devs:
Since your app’s strength is how many ways it can be used, there are some little changes that would increase that greatly. 

- Allow custom rating systems for symptoms and other things. (e.g 1-10/3-46 or whatever other number scale versus a type in option versus an emoji option etc). You already have all of these features but only certain features can use it (only heath measurements can use type in, only symptoms can use 1-4 etc). If all the features that it makes sense for could be customized as to what they’re using the app would be much more dynamic. 
- Allow us to customize which features we use. (Think strategies/features from Amazing Marvin). This would be become more useful as you add more things so it doesn’t clutter the homepage of the people who don’t care for certain features. 

This one is more difficult but I think it would help a lot as I know you get complaints about the homepage setup sometimes:

-Allow us to further customize our homepage. I would like to be able to group things together that aren’t necessarily from the same feature. (e.g. put a health measurement and a factor in the same group, or a symptom and a medication etc. rather than having all factors together and all custom ratings together) This would allow us to create a custom process for logging as well as a design that we personally like.

reviews.title: THE BEST Symptom Tracker for chronic illness
reviews.text: I take a whole laundry list of meds that change frequently, and I just found out I'm autistic, and I have been battling major depression, PTSD, and anxiety for years. I also have chronic migraines from a severe head injury. Because of my autism, it's been difficult to communicate how I'm doing to my therapists and psychiatrists and doctors, and often I was not believed about the severity of my symptoms, or accused of not taking my medication, or told that my sleep or energy is better than I think it is. Now I have EMPIRICAL DATA all gathered in one place that provides an accurate assessment of my moods, symptoms both mental and physical, everything all in one place. My only complaint is that I wish you could time stamp EVERYTHING, not just medication times and mood and energy but also factors and symptoms instead of being limited to 4 time ranges because I'd like to see if a short-term intervention works and right now I can only see that I listen to relaxing music when I get anxious, but not whether I feel less anxious after listening to relaxing music. reviews.title: Changed my life, everything I've always wanted!
reviews.text:
I've never written an app review before because I'm never consistent enough when using apps. It's been over 6  months of using Bearable and it's everything I've always wanted in a health tracking app. I've used several health tracking, todo, mood tracking apps and this has by far exceeded all my expectations.

I love how customizable and flexible it is! Many apps don't even allow you to add your own tags. I also love how simple the app is, no frills. Design wise – it's so easy to grok and read. The colors are just right and not overwhelming. Even though there's a ton of things going on in this app, it's easy to navigate. 

Love that it syncs to Apple health. I'm able to also connect other data (e.g. Oura data) from Apple Health to Bearable so I have all my health metrics in one place.

I use this mainly to track factors/medication affecting my anxiety/depression but it's also become a habit tracker! I love that I can use the calendar view to see how many days I've done a certain "factor" or action. Doing this daily also just helps me be present and reflect on my day in a quick and accesible way! 

The insights are not as helpful for me but I'd say that about any health tracking app – the obvious things are always true (exercise, eat well, get sun, sleep well, etc) but it's nice to see the trends over time in case you're going through some big life changes.

Thank you so much for creating this app. Seriously!!!

reviews.title: Literally changed my life.
reviews.text: To start off with, this is the first app review that I have ever written - and I stopped using Bearable consistently probably a year ago, but occasionally it weighs on my heart to let others know my success story with Bearable. I had struggled with severe major depression, generalized anxiety, PTSD, and OCD (and still do, to a lesser extent) for close to a decade. I decided to invest in Bearable because anxiety had begun leaving me completely unable to function every single day — like literally spent a week in bed just incessantly panicking. Cue setting up Bearable, painstakingly inputting every detail I could think of. I found after several months of use that many of the things that I thought were “right” were actually leaving me in absolute wreckage, while my partner and his family were consistently bring my mood up SUBSTANTIALLY. Seeing the numbers laid out encouraged me to make the difficult decision of leaving what I now identify was a cult. It helped me cut ties with abusive situations that had trapped my family for generations. It helped me learn what joy was after years of hospital visits, SH episodes, panic attacks, and starvation. I am now living my best life and will look to Bearable again occasionally for answers to menial health concerns. This app changed my life and I would almost definitely not be here without it.

reviews.title: GAME CHANGER
reviews.text: I rarely write reviews for apps, but felt like I needed to knowing this app could help someone feel more empowered in their health journey. I was recently diagnosed with ADHD as an adult, and I used this app to begin tracking my symptoms I was experiencing to help communicate to my doctors how serious of a problem this was for me. Now after getting the diagnosis, I’ve been using it to help my brain see my health as a priority. The data and insights I get from it also helps me to stop living in autopilot and be more intentional about the decisions I’m making for my health. I wish I could say more, but at this point just get the app and try it for yourself. Even without the premium account, it was VERY helpful. Wishing you all the best on your health journey. 🙏🏽

I love that it also includes non-medical tracking as well (e.g mood, habits, major life events, meditation and sleep). I can track my daily meds, mood, sleep, and symptoms all in the same app! The only negative would be that it is SO detailed, and there’s SO much you can do, it can sometimes be overwhelming, which can deter you from following the regime.

reviews.title: Islands of data impair effectiveness
reviews.text:
What you are looking for in a tracker of any kind is for it to be as effortless as possible, meaning taking data from various sources and making sense of it without you having to add data manually. 
That’s what we like about the Apple Watch for instance it is capturing so much data just being on your wrist. 
The problem is when applications capture the same set of data, do it manually, and don’t collaborate. So as an IOS user I have updated my mood status (sporadically, because there are things happening in your life distracting you from updating an app) and now this application is asking me to do the same, on different metrics… why can’t bearable use Apple health data or the other way around. Given this is one of the core value of the app, correlating events to moods you end up having scattered data which is not exploited. 
I also have an app Welltory that captures biometrically my energy level but I have to enter it manually here. 
So not a problem of the app per say but just lack of data integration. All these apps should work together to better collaborate!

reviews.title: Decent tracking but insights not statistically significant
reviews.text: This app is very customizable and lets you track a lot. Generally very good for input, but i think struggles with visualization and analysis—better to export data and do that on your own. There are many visualization options, but all are much too limited or not useful (for me). The app also has “insights” and experiments about how different things you log are correlated, but there is not much statistical information, only the average and nothing on sample size or statistical significance, which makes it impossible to rely on.

reviews.title: Phenomenal
reviews.text:
I have tried a lot of different methods for tracking symptoms. But this one takes the cake. Before hand, sitting down and writing it every day wasn’t easy especially on heavy fatigue/drowsiness days. This app has quickly become a favorite of mine. It took a little bit to explore all the features but I’ve finally got the hang of it. I’ve tried apps, planners, and the like for so long. None of them were up to par with my needs except this one. I got the premium version and I can say it is actually worth it. 

Being able to visually see my symptoms fluctuate and understand how they’re affected by certain things is such a big plus. The nutrition tracking ability is also great because it’s simple & not calorie based. I can tag it as a heavy fruit veggie day Vs not. 

As someone with interest in app development, UI/UX design, etc : good job! The app is fairly easy to navigate, things are clear, and the layout works. Whoever is behind building this app deserves every dollar they make. I know how difficult these features and the like can be to put together. So kudos.

Onto things I could see being added / enjoy : - urination tracker ; some of us pee a whole lot and it could be useful for doctor appointments. 

That’s all the feedback I have for now. Honestly I have major gratitude for the people that put this together. I wanted to build something similar but never managed to due to getting sick on and off.

reviews.title: Wonderful app for all health care tracking!
reviews.text: Bearable is a beautifully crafted app that helps me track so many of my different metrics and then compiles them for me to view in an easy to understand way. I love it! You can add as much or as little information about yourself and your day as you like. The layout is pleasing to the eye and the more I use it the more I wsnt to add more info so I can see my trends. It's reasonably priced too for a subscription. Check it out, you'll agree that it's great for you, too! 🩷 Thanks, devs!!

reviews.text: I would like it if this app fit the screen of the iPad. I want this app to be able to login across multiple devices.

reviews.title: Loving it
reviews.text: This app is exactly what I need to track progression/regression of symptoms and to correlate with my mood and and pain. I’ve lived with chronic pain for years and used to track these things in a notebook by hand. This app is so much quicker and easier. And has so much to offer even with the free version!

reviews.title: Finally got an answer for my health!!
reviews.text:
As someone with chronic pain and illness, I have been to so many doctors and they never knew what was wrong despite multiple tests. After tracking signs and symptoms for two months, I finally found what was wrong and my doctor started me on meds for it. I haven’t had that pain since. 

It is wonderful to finally know what’s wrong with you and get the answers. It just took me logging *all* of the things BUT thankfully it was all in one place

reviews.title: Pretty Fantastic
reviews.text: I was impressed with the ease to operate and the sense of accountability and motivation it invokes. I highly recommend.

reviews.title: Comprehensive Symptoms & Lifestyle Tracker
reviews.text:
Not only does Bearable offer a whole bunch of symptoms tracking categories, but you can also integrate lifestyle & habit tracking (everything is optional of course). 
For example, you can track hydration, outdoor time, screen time, socialization, food, exercise. But the best part is that every category & it’s subcategories is editable, hideable and moveable so that you can designate names (w or w.o emojis) & organize lists so that what you need to see first is at top (this is key for meds & vitamins). A great product, I highly recommend.

reviews.text: Just started using this a couple weeks ago, but so far I really like it. The interface wasn’t totally intuitive at first - it’s not always obvious where to log a particular activity/symptom. But after you get the hang of it, it’s easier. The customization is great - I can remove items I don’t want to track or add missing ones. I’m looking forward to seeing the reports soon of how my symptoms correlate with my behaviors.

It also helps me to acknowledge how prevalent each of my symptoms actually are which can be important when you’ve dealt with issues for a long time and start to brush things off because you’re so used to them. I do wish the extra notes part were included in the free version, but not a big deal. Would 100% recommend!!

You get nearly every input for the free version, which is awesome. You just unlock all of the charts and analysis once you pay for premium.

reviews.title: Great for Doctor Appointments
reviews.text:
After a visit to ER I was asked by my Neurologist to keep track of my symptoms. I found Bearable from an AD on social media- and thought I’d try it. It hasn’t ever been this easy to keep track of symptoms/pains, daily activities, nutrition, and moods ALL IN ONE PLACE.
I’m able to track when I see what doctor, when I get tests done, when I take what med and how much. As well as what symptoms/pains come up and what I was doing around that time. 
It helps me keep track so when I see my specialist, I am able to reflect and give them an accurate timeline. Able to answer their questions confidently and in depth.
I only have access to the free version- and honestly it’s all I need. 
Absolutely thrilled to have this app!!!

reviews.title: Mixed bag
reviews.text:
Cute mascot. Despite a lengthy privacy policy assuring you they aren't doing anything shady, at the very bottom it tells you that they're giving your email address to Facebook and Google to "find more customers like you", so be sure to sign up with Apple and use the "hide email" feature.

The onboarding is well-intentioned but annoying (far too long due to an unnecessary, unskippable "customization" questionnaire). It can supposedly import data like heart rate from Health but it's not in there by default, does not ask during onboarding, and how to sync it is unclear. The UI is visually attractive but not intuitive, and it needs a lot of work on the usability front-- for example, you cannot close the 'choose the main symptoms you want to track' window without closing the entire app. It's also one of those """free""" apps that are actually unusable after the subscription trial period, because the entire insights tab is paywalled.

All of that said, it's the only app I could find that's trying to do what it's doing, and it deserves credit for that and the cute visual design.

reviews.text: This app is perfect in all ways except one fatal flaw, I can’t track my symptoms with exacts times of the day! I can do bowel movements and mood, but I have to generalize the symptoms in buckets throughout the day. I’ve been trying to figure out what’s been causing my fatigue for the past 2 years and having the option to track more granular trends in time would be very very helpful. I’m a premium user but going to have to find a new app that offers this feature which is really unfortunate cause the UI/UX is amazing on Bearable

reviews.title: A godsend for tracking complex health matters
reviews.text:
In the process of trying to tend to multiple overlapping short- and long- term physical and mental health matters, including a challenging diagnostic path for a possible rare genetic condition, I realized that keeping a notes file with general observations wasn’t cutting it anymore. It became abundantly clear that I’m going to need much more granular data to not only help parse my complicated presentation, but also to advocate for myself with providers and insurance. I researched multiple health and lifestyle tracking apps before landing on Bearable and giving it a trial week. I didn’t need a week, though — It was clear on the same day that I downloaded it that it was a keeper. 

Bearable offers a flexible system for tracking not just symptoms but a whole range of lifestyle factors that influence wellbeing. Its default set-up is pretty robust to start with and may serve many users well without much tweaking. That said, it was super easy and intuitive to use its defaults as a jumping off point for adding custom factors to track (i.e. very specific symptoms such as left hand tingling/numbness vs right, and daily activities specific to my life, like how much VR headset use). 

After you get a few days logged, the app starts to provide correlations between the tracked items. While correlation isn’t causation, seeing these connections offers plenty of insight to allow for greater self-awareness and to help guide inquiries to providers. In under a week it has given me new awareness of some semi-regular activities that appear to positively impact my mental health, so now I can explore the connection intentionally. Never would have put two and two together on my own. 

Perhaps the best part is discovering how much the (small!) Bearable team works with its users to make further developments. Multiple platforms exist to interact with the community of Bearable users and the creators, where requests and ideas are shared and bounced back and forth with the creators as they make developments. I’ve never seen a company walk the talk SO thoroughly on their commitment to being user driven. 

This might be a weirdly long and effusive review 😅, but it’s impacted me that much.

Thank you so much, Bearable team. Your app, and your palpable care, have given me a practice tool *and* a dash of empowerment and optimism about my own health. 💗

reviews.title: A lot more app than I expected, yet also less
reviews.text:
I saw that Apple Health added the ability to track an assortment of symptoms, and I have the occasional headache or stuffy nose … so I went looking for an app which might simplify my ability to record my symptoms to Apple Health.

I suppose what I visualized was my telling the app “Oh, I have a headache!” and the app asking me “How bad is it?” and my telling it “Mild,” and the app saying “Shall I ask you again in an hour how you’re feeling?” and my saying “Sure,” and the app waiting an hour and then asking “What’s up?” and my saying “Oh, I’ve been feeling fine for 15 minutes,” and the app replying “Okay then!” and recording into Apple Health “Headache - mild; from 1:10 to 1:55 p.m. on so-and-so date.” If I was lucky, I thought the app might also record to Apple Health that I’d taken two acetaminophen.

But mostly I just wanted it to write my symptoms to Apple Health, so that other apps could read them from there, or so that I might include symptoms — and their time and date — in an overall printout of Apple Health for my doctor, elementary stuff.

This app is not that!! This app is so-o-o-o-oo detailed, like it gets really granular in terms of the things it tracks and charts. If you’re inclined to record a lot of data into it, I suppose it could help you spot correlations between symptoms and the events surrounding those symptoms. It seems designed for people with truly debilitating chronic illnesses, who may need help narrowing down exactly what’s making their lives so unlivable.

And it may be great for people with debilitating chronic illness — I would not know, I’m a pretty healthy dude who intended to be a casual user. For me, for what little I needed, this app quickly overwhelmed me … and the subscription price, ye cats! For my intended casual level of use, this kind of pricing seems stratospheric. So it may be great for some people, but it’s not the app for me.

All of that being said, though, I’m quite surprised it DOES NOT sync symptoms to Apple Health. That’s quite an oversight. I wish apps which sync with Apple Health were required to specify in their App Store description what info it is exactly that they sync: this would save users lots of time. This app does READ a tremendous amount of info FROM Apple Health, but it does NOT write your symptoms TO Apple Health.

So I give it three stars in terms of its utility to me: it looks like it works, it’s extraordinarily detailed, it’s just not what I need right now, and it does NOT do the one thing I’d hoped it would do. But for you, if you have a life-upending chronic illness, it may be a five-star app or even a six-star app. Luckily for me I’m in good shape, and to be honest, I hope I continue NOT needing this app.

If the day comes that I do, though, I would still be disappointed if they hadn’t added the ability to WRITE symptoms TO Apple Health for possible integration with other apps; this seems like the whole point of having a centralized repository of health information!

reviews.title: Love it, wish there were two additional features
reviews.text:
I have been looking for an app like this for AGES and imagine my surprise when an Instagram add pointed me towards one that actually works. This is what data should be for. It takes away so much stress for me that I don’t have to be the one trying to unpack what is leading to chronic pain flare ups, I can just be diligent about logging everything in and it would give me metrics. 

This is such a helpful app I’d like to hope that maybe the creators would take some suggestions from people who have benefited from using it and add two features: a food log and the ability to enter periods of disrupted sleep. I’d like to see if there’s an association between WHAT I eat and how I feel and it would be really useful to be able to keep that in the same app. I’d also like to be able to indicate in the app if I was awake between 4am-5am, rather than only be able to list the total time from when I initially went to sleep to when I started my day, as I think that makes a huge difference in how I feel the next day. 

Thank you for making an app that people with chronic pain actually need, for making it integrated with apple health, and for not forgetting about us menstruating folk out there.

reviews.title: Pretty interface but too structured
reviews.text: Doesnt work for my needs, which is mostly tracking pain and activities that may be related. Zero ability to make any kind of notes, and little ability to customize the interface and data gathered. I found a much better one for my particular focus.

reviews.title: It’s great but sync issues are a bummer
reviews.text:
I downloaded this earlier this week and really thought it was a great idea, and figured the annual membership was affordable compared to other apps. But sadly the app won’t sync to Apple health, and I really wished it synced with a nutrition app like my fitness pal, especially because I’m in the process of trying to figure out food sensitivities. I’ve tried all the tricks like disconnecting and resynching and uninstalling. 

I’ve had a lot of issues with how Apple health is designed and what it does and doesn’t include. Was hoping bearable could bridge that gap, but seems like I’m out of luck. 

I still plan on using it, since it’s still the best option out there, and it’s good at what it does do! I love how customizable the symptom trackers are!

reviews.title: Love this app!
reviews.text: I really have enjoyed using this app. It’s easy to track your symptoms, mood, pains, and everything else! I wish they had a lock screen or home screen widget though to make it easier to log info.

reviews.title: An app that can finally track all my health challenges
reviews.text: I’ve tried a couple of apps that tracked symptoms but only the ones that came with the app and the list of symptoms wasn’t as comprehensive. Other apps also don’t have lifestyle tracking, events, and a way to customize your tracking in six hour time intervals which is great for making health correlations. I like the customization, and especially the ability to choose which metrics to compare so you can make relevant assumptions about what activities you’re doing that are impacting your health the most. I’ve had some new symptoms come up lately and I’m hoping that tracking these symptoms and giving the report to my doctors will be very useful in getting an accurate diagnosis.

reviews.title: Fantastic autoimmune app!
reviews.text: I tried several before landing on Bearable. I like the flexibility of this app and being able to record several times a day since my symptoms change by the hour. Also the cute bear makes me smile.

reviews.title: 7 day free trial?
reviews.text: I was charged for a 7-day free trial. I signed up on December 14 and cancelled on day 7, December 21 and was still charged. If it’s a 7 day free trial, should I not be charged on the 8th day??? I am not happy at all and do not recommend this app at all. Not a happy customer. Buyer beware.

reviews.title: 1-4 Pain Scale
reviews.text: App would be more helpful if it allowed pain to be measured on a 1-10 scale, not 1-4. Most Doctors and hospitals use a 1-10 scale.

reviews.title: I’ve been dreaming of this app for years
reviews.text: This is exactly what I’ve been wanting for years. So excited that a talented team built it right! Extensible, customizable, intuitive, and cute to boot. A+ to whoever came up with the name.

reviews.title: Genuine Review
reviews.text: Bearable is one of the few apps I deem worthy of a subscription. The app is genuinely amazing. The health data is stored privately, It’s very customizable, and they’re transparent with what features they’re working on adding, considering adding, and aren’t adding. I use it to keep track of the medications I take, it makes it so much easier to remember when I’ve taken what, and at the exact time I’ve taken it. It’s super easy to log symptoms too if you want to keep track of your symptom’s severity, and can add custom symptoms too. Does it do absolutely everything? No. But does it do amazingly at the other things? YES! I love the app.

reviews.title: Useful app
reviews.text: As a person with chronic conditions, this app is very useful and helpful to track symptoms and other factors every day. The days can be broken into time blocks (pre, am, mid, pm) which I really like. I only use the free version and I still love the app.

reviews.title: Love this app (updated)
reviews.text:
Edit: Thank you SO MUCH for adding the ability to enter times in 12 hour am/pm format!! 

I love having a central place to keep track of my symptoms and things I did each day. It is a great tool to use in the evening and reflect back on the day. It allows me to look at trends over time, which is helpful. The app has a very user-friendly layout and cute design and I would definitely recommend!

reviews.title: Most comprehensive symptom tracker and affordable
reviews.text: You can customize it and it was a affordable price for the year what I’ve seen some symptom trackers charge for a month.   The customization and affordability and having everything in one place and it connects to your health apps.  This app was beautifully designed and I hope they keep the price the same or lower to make it more accessible for more people who could benefit from it.  Also being able to use on my computer as well would be nice!  I love that you offer a week trial before getting charged.  I kept it after the week I love it so much.  Highly recommend. It can help you notice trends so you can help yourself

reviews.text:

But I love, Love,LOVE it, so far. If your body does weird things and your trying to find a correlation I highly recommend this app.

reviews.title: Best Symptom Tracker around!
reviews.text:
This is by far the best symptom tracker I have ever found, and I have been using it for several years. I originally was looking for a way to track chronic pain/headaches, but could only find migraine apps and I didn’t have common triggers. I love that this app is customizable to each user, and you can track specifically for you! I also love the calendar feature that shows how many days out of the month you experience specific symptoms, and the notes section available under each symptom. 

Overall, I would HIGHLY recommend this app, especially if you have less common or undiagnosed issues.

reviews.title: Where has this app been all my life!
reviews.text: So I have used just about every tracking app you can imagine and this is hands down the the first that was worth the trouble of getting it set up. I’m a nurse and use the FAM so I have a lot of experience tracking health data and this is the best symptom tracker I’ve ever tried. The only thing I would suggest adding is basic basically body temperature tracking features. It should be easy to add since you already have a way to track temperature (and Apple Watch and Ora integration which is a must for getting meaningful temperature data).

reviews.title: Grateful for 30 Days on Bearable!
reviews.text:
I've struggled with a variety of illness' and symptoms since I was a child. Before Bearable trying to keep track of everything was always difficult and I found myself getting lost in symptoms. 
I've tried other symptom logging apps but they were either too open ended or too rigid on what the symptoms and intensity should be and neither matched up to what I needed. Normally I have trouble sticking with things but I got the email today that i'm 30 days on bearable, right after logging my symptoms into the app! 
Im very grateful for bearable because now all of that chaos is behind me. I can easily log my symptoms, nutrition, water, sleep and more with a few pushes of buttons. I love how customizable the app is, you can add or take away common symptoms and rate the severity of discomfort. 
I also appreciate how the data is organized that's collected, I can easily see what my symptoms have been for each category organized by date. This has greatly helped with doctors appointments and remembering exactly when symptoms began or were difficult, intensity, and other factors from that time.

reviews.title: Great app

reviews.text: This app replaces three others I had, is much smoother to use, and includes easy to document, easy to access details. You can individualize your information in endless ways and it has genuinely helped me have a better quality of life.

I’ve seen dramatic results in last 6 weeks simply due to the awareness and discipline of tracking mood etc.  Support team was very responsive in helping me resolve a technical issue. reviews.title: Great!
reviews.text: I just downloaded this app to help me take better care of my self care as well as be able to track my mental health and boost it up with the progression of time. I would love to be able to have a widget so i can see some of my goals/tasks that i need to get done!

reviews.title: Worth every penny
reviews.text: If you’re like me and you’re dealing with health problems, you’re probably doing so many things all at once just to see if something helps and find some relief. Medications, exercise, therapy, fill in the blank. And then you experience a setback and you think “Are any of the things I’m doing even helping? Am I making any progress?” This app takes care of that for you. The premium version is so customizable. You can input any habit, activity, symptom, medication, etc. that you want. And the automatic correlations that the app finds between your habits and outcomes is so helpful. I’ve only been using the app for two weeks, and I can already see that when I go for walks, my weird leg pain improves. So that motivates me to go for more walks. I probably wouldn’t have figured that out on my own because there are just so many variables that go into my day. It’s just little things like that, and having that knowledge, that makes a huge difference in your health journey. I’m withholding one star because wish I could track my cycle. I manually created factors for each phase of the cycle, but I wish it was a built in feature. Our hormones really have a huge impact on every aspect of our life, and it would help me and a lot of women to have that data. And it’s something we could easily show our GYN too for them to be able to say “yeah, that’s normal,” or “you get extremely depressed when you’re menstruating, that’s not healthy and we need to look into that.” But other than that I love the app and know that it’s going to be very beneficial the more I use it.

reviews.title: One of the best I've found
reviews.text: With a long-term, chronic condition that really needs a lot of tracking to see patterns and to discern what is helping, Bearable is about the best app around to track EVERYTHING in one place.  Even the free version is very robust, so you can really use it and not just try it out. I really appreciate this app.

If you back out you get no service from the app and they get no money but they do walk away with a LOT of very personal information.

reviews.text: Great ap! Easy to use and I can track things like pollen, mold, food and fatigue for histimine intolerance. Thanks! And love the reminders

reviews.text:
I’ve been trying multiple apps to track food, symptoms, and medications. This one seemed like it had all these features but it doesn’t let you track basics like protein, fat, and carb intake.

reviews.text: I never write reviews when they ask for it. I’m sick. I don’t have the time or energy to write reviews. If you’re here reading this review, I’m sure you’re in the same boat. You’re sick too. You are weak and tired too. You don’t have time or energy. But this app is incredible. It doesn’t take time. It saves time. It makes time. It makes joy. It makes ease. It makes me smile. It has a bear on it. Trust me. It’s well executed and brilliantly thought out, even the free version which is what I’m using. I’ve used it for a week and even with my cognitive impairments it’s incredibly intuitive and easy to use. I LOVE it. Genuinely. It’s so easy to use, to customize and personalize, to track, to make your own for any and all your health needs. I’ve shown it to everyone. In one week it’s made all 3 of my doctors appointments go so much smoother. It’s made taking and tracking all 15 daily medications go by so much easier. Tracking my food too to make sure I eat despite forgetting and the nausea and the appetite being gone. It has the ability to remind you to do things. Take medicine for example. Tracking my many symptoms too. Even the little gratitude tracker is a nice bonus. And the mood tracker is a nice bonus to have me consciously think about how I’m feeling emotionally not just physically. All of it is brilliant. I love that I can add in my own symptoms and my own emotions, for when I feel ennui or emotionally energized or on fire or proud, or symptoms like ‘senility’ or other things that don’t come pre-set. It’s all just so incredible and I could go on and on. I wish I could pay for it to use all its goodness but the free version is nice too. Just to track what I do. Do yourself a favor and just download this, if there’s anything at all up with your health. Yeah, just do it. Make yourself beary happy.

reviews.title: Missing some common sense features
reviews.text:
I’ve been on the hunt for a tracking app that combines rich app-generated insights with maximum user customizability. Bearable nails the first; their analysis is comprehensive and user-friendly—though without the ability to share or export insights, they hinder users’ ability to maximize the usefulness of those insights.  

Bearable is also great at building in the ability for users to customize *what* they track. Where the app falls short on user customization though is in *how* we track. This includes customizing the mood scale, colors, rating levels (none-unbearable), whether a factor is considered positive or negative in the analysis, and whether it makes sense for a symptom or factor to have multiple ratings/day or have it apply to the whole day (e.g., a symptom like acne or a factor like “out of town” doesn’t change 4 times a day). 

But these are relatively minor and non-disruptive to tracking compared to my biggest issue here: not being able to modify the time windows on which all tracking is based. (For non-Bearable users, these are 12am-6am, 6am-12pm, 12pm-6pm, and 6pm-12am.) As a “night owl,” it feels like a huge chunk of data is missing because the default times assume my day ends at midnight. Including those symptoms or factors in the 12am-6am window for the following day messes with that day’s average and is inaccurate. I never wake up before 6am, so I never put anything in the “pre” box, meaning I’m only really tracking 18 hours of the day, with everything that happens from 12am-bedtime completely left out. I’ve considered mentally changing the time windows but that would be incredibly inconvenient for an app I’m paying a subscription for. 

Like most user-submitted suggestions, this has been on the feature roadmap for ages and it’s unclear whether it’ll ever happen.

reviews.title: Exactly what I was hoping for and more!
reviews.text:
I’m fairly new to a complicated chronic illness and learning how to manage it has been really confusing and hard. 

It’s so hard to know what unexpected factors might be exacerbating problems, and the stakes feel really high for drawing connections as fast as possible to avoid further damage. 

I really wanted a way to track EVERYTHING, like every small bit of data I could, to see if sense could be made of it, and was thinking it would be nice if there was an app for it but didn’t feel hopeful about finding something as comprehensive as I was dreaming of.

So I have been delighted over and over again with how comprehensively Bearable has already solved this problem! The fact that it was made by someone with a chronic illness really shows, because this is so thorough and so easy to modify. I’m just using the free version and it’s blowing my mind, I can’t even imagine how much MORE comprehensive it gets with the premium upgrade!

Highly recommended. It’s really great and exactly what I wanted and more.
